hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=\log_3x$ and $g(x)=1.5$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and the solution of $f(x)=g(x)$ can be found by looking for their intersection points.

options.alt: A logarithmic function graph and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph increases from left to right through points (one, zero) and (three, one) going towards infinity. The asymptote is at x equals zero. The horizontal line is at y equals one and one half and intersects the logarithmic function graph at one point.

hints.content:
The graphs intersect where the $x$-coordinate is approximately $5$.

[[☃ image 1]]
